 By WRAL News staff
 Voters have two more days to cast their ballots early and in person — ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections — and to register to vote if they missed previous registration deadlines. 
 A total of 370 early, in-person voting sites opened Oct. 15 and are scheduled to close Saturday. Voters can find their local sites online at the state or county election board websites. Voters can cast their ballots at any early voting location in the county where they're registered, rather than having to visit their assigned Election Day precinct. 
 Other WRAL Top Stories
 Before heading to the polls, voters should check early-voting location hours, bring an acceptable photo identification and make sure their registration information is up to date. The exact days and hours for polling places vary by county.
 Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Polls on that day will be open from 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.
 In past elections, most North Carolinians have voted during early voting rather than on Election Day itself. 
 Through Thursday, almost 2.4 million North Carolinians had cast early ballots in this year’s election — either by mail or at an early voting site. That’s about 30% of all eligible voters in the state. Early voting is up about 34% compared with the same period in the 2022 election cycle, state data shows.
 Where and when can I vote? 
 Wake County voters will have 18 early voting locations to choose from, including sites in Raleigh, Apex and Garner.
 Among them are Abbott's Creek Community Center in north Raleigh, Chavis Community Center in southeast Raleigh, Apex Community Center and Avery Street Recreation Center in Garner.
 Voters don't need to pick the location closest to their home. Any of the county's early voting sites will work.
 Wake County's early voting hours are:
 Friday: 8 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. 
 Saturday: 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. 
 Don’t live in Wake County? Voters can find which polling location matches with their address and check locations and hours using the state's early voting site lookup .
 Some may also want to double-check which days they can vote, since those aren't the same every year. This year, election officials in  many but not all counties ended Sunday voting .
 Election officials say the first and last days of early voting are often the busiest.
 Can I still register to vote? 
 You can still register and vote during early in-person voting. However, for people who plan to vote by mail or on Election Day itself, it's too late: the registration deadline for those options is over.
 Voters who want to register to vote or update their information during early voting must be an eligible voter and provide proof of their current address, such as a driver's license, utility bill, bank statement or government document.
 They must have lived in their county for at least 30 days before Election Day.
 Same-day registration is not available for most voters on Nov. 3.
 What should I bring? 
 Bring an acceptable photo ID . Accepted IDs include a North Carolina driver's license, U.S. passport and certain state-issued or approved student IDs.
 Most IDs must be unexpired or expired for one year or less. Different rules apply to voters 65 and older, military IDs and certain other forms of identification.
 Forgot yours? You can still cast a provisional ballot and bring an acceptable ID to your county elections board no later than 12 p.m. on Nov. 10.
 Voters who cannot provide ID may also request an exemption to the rules by filling out a form if they can claim one of multiple acceptable reasons for not having an ID. However, state officials recently rewrote the rules to make it easier to throw out people's ballots if election administrators decide they don't believe a voters' claim on that exemption form.
 Can I bring my phone? 
 Yes, to look up candidate information. But taking a photo of your completed ballot is illegal , and voters cannot use their phones to communicate with others while inside the voting booth.
 What about voting by mail? 
 Voters who already received an absentee ballot can return it to an election official at an early voting location in their county, to their county elections board or by mail. You can track its progress through the mail using the state's BallotTrax app .
 And those who change their minds don't have to vote by mail even if they requested a mail-in ballot. They can ask elections officials to cancel it and vote in person instead, as long as they don't vote twice. Or they can fill out the mail-in ballot and hand-deliver it, either to an early voting poll place before the end of early voting Saturday at 3 p.m., or after that, by delivering it to their county elections board office on Monday or Tuesday — before polls close at at 7:30 p.m.
 A relatively new state law eliminated the post-election grace period for ballots to still be counted if they arrived a few days late, as long as they were postmarked on or before Election Day. Now, any ballots that arrive after polls close at 7:30 p.m. Tuesday will be thrown out, no matter when they were put in the mail.
 What if I need assistance? 
 Curbside voting is available for voters who cannot enter a polling place without physical assistance because of age or disability. Voters may also request help from poll workers or bring an eligible person to assist them.
 What's on my ballot? 
 Voters will decide races for Congress, the state legislature, courts and local offices, along with ballot questions that vary by location. To see a sample ballot with your specific candidates and ballot questions, use the state's voter lookup tool .
